title: Stage Operational Data Before You Model It
objective: Design a staging schema that preserves source grain and a warehouse schema with an explicit grain, keys, and one slowly-changing-attribute decision — without turning the work into an analytics report.
whyThisMatters: A pipeline that writes straight into a 'clean' table hides the source. Staging is the audit trail; the warehouse is the contracted shape. Getting that split wrong is how silent rewrites and unreplayable loads start.
evidence: A source-to-target map covering every source field
Committed SQL DDL that creates staging and warehouse schemas and tables
An SCD decision note that includes one query that would be wrong under the rejected choice
A captured listing of the created schemas and tables
Reflection notes answering the task questions
acceptanceCriteria: The source-to-target map lists every source field as either landed in a named staging column or explicitly dropped with a one-line reason.
A comment or note on the warehouse fact or primary table states the grain in one sentence.
One changing attribute has a written SCD type-1 versus type-2 decision plus one example query that returns a wrong answer under the rejected choice.
PostgreSQL schemas named staging and warehouse exist, and a captured \d or information_schema listing shows at least one table in each.
